feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (lead 0.05 m, track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, 5 sensors) reached s-bend progress 0.29, the best so far. Iteration 1 (lead 0.03 m, track 0.10 m) dropped to 0.18, and iteration 2 (7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.03 m) dropped to 0.04 with line loss 0. Sensing reach is therefore not the limit, and the shorter lead has coincided with each drop. This candidate restores the lead to 0.05 m and lowers yaw inertia, which should help if the failure is overshoot. Because lower inertia can also increase overshoot, I added kd 0.6 to the controller so the damping is not left to chance. Interpret the next race as follows. If s-bend progress reaches 0.25 or more and line_loss_events stays 0, keep this geometry and move to a narrower track of 0.08 m to test turn authority. If s-bend progress is still below 0.25 with line loss 0, the cause is turn response, not geometry, so ask for a lighter-inertia comparison at lead 0.05 m with the track unchanged. If line_loss_events rises to 1 or more, the outer sensors are losing the tape at this lead, so widen to +/-0.07 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress reaches 0.25 or more with line_loss_events at 0 and max_error still near 0.06 m, try wheel_track 0.08 m with the lead at 0.05 m and mass 0.6 kg, since iteration 0's 0.12 m track was not the limit and turn authority is the next test.

If line_loss_events reach 1 or more on the s-bend or slalom, widen the outer sensors to x = +/-0.07 m with 16 mm footprints, since iteration 1 showed loss near 0.0565 m offset and iteration 2 showed the 0.06 m edge is still at risk.

If s-bend progress stays below 0.25 with line loss at 0 and the lead at 0.05 m, hold the geometry and report the controller's kd and base_speed response, rather than changing the lead again, since iteration 0 at lead 0.05 m reached 0.29 and the lead has not been the cause of the drops.
